newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Fidel Ramos says a 240 million peso damage suit filed by business tycoon Lucio Tan against Internal Revenue Commissioner Liwayway Vinzons Chato will not affect the government's tax evasion cases against Tan. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- President Fidel Ramos dismisses speculation that the appointment of retired military officers to civilian posts is a prelude to his plan to extend his stay in power. (ALL PAPERS)
- The opposition is firming up plans to bring together three political parties under one umbrella for the 1998 presidential election, Senate president Ernesto Maceda says. (MANILA TIMES)

- The Presidential Commission on Good Government has urged food and beverage conglomerate San Miguel Corp to renegotiate the terms of its merger deal with Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd of Australia even as it voted in favour of the deal. (ALL PAPERS)
- Telecom giant Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co has promised its interconnection problems with other phone companies will be resolved in the second quarter of the year (MANILA TIMES)

- Isla Communications Co Inc says it will pull out of the Telecommunications Infrastructure Corp of the Philippines, a firm set up to build an alternative nationwide telecom backbone to the one run by the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Stockholders of Philippines Savings Bank approve the increase in the bank's authorised capital stock to 4.25 billion pesos from three billion pesos. (ALL PAPERS)
